purpose: Consolidated evidence for preferred commentary or qualified Greek review; no outbound contact or publication has occurred.

greek.source_text: ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν. οὔτε ἐπιβουλὴν φοβηθήσομαι, οὐ δώροις κολακευθήσομαι. ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ δόξειέν μοι ποτὲ τὰ διδόμενά μοι τῶν κηρυγμάτων βιβλία μὴ ἀληθῆ εἶναι, οὐδ’ οὕτως μεταδώσω, ἀλλ’ ἀποδώσω. ἀποδημῶν δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ αὐτὰ κομίσω, ἅπερ ἂν τύχω κεκτημένος· εἰ δὲ μὴ βουληθῶ μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ αὐτὰ περιφέρειν, ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκίας μου εἶναι αὐτὰ οὐκ ἐάσω, ἀλλὰ τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ μου τῷ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχοντι πίστιν καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν αὐτῶν ὁρμωμένῳ παρακαταθήσομαι. εἰ δὲ καὶ τύχοι με νοσῆσαι καὶ τὸν θάνατον ὑποπτεύσαι, ἐὰν ἄτεκνος ὦ, ὁμοίως ποιήσω. ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ τελευτῶ τέκνον ἔχων οὐκ ἄξιον ἢ μηδέπω δυνάμενον, ὁμοίως ποιήσω· τῷ γὰρ ἐπισκόπῳ μου παρακαταθήσομαι·, ἵνα εἰ μὲν τύχοι, ἐφ’ ἡλικίας γενόμενος, ἄξιος εἶναι τῆς πίστεως, ὡς πατρῴαν παρακαταθήκην τῷ τέκνῳ ἀποδώσει, κατὰ τὸν τῆς διαμαρτυρίας λόγον.

held_passages.provisional_english: “Otherwise—not even a child or a brother or a friend or anyone ever related to me in any other way, if indeed he is unworthy—not to pass on any of this as a favor, since it is not proper. I will not fear a plot, nor will I be won over by gifts. But even if at some point the books of the proclamations given to me seem to me not to be true, not even then will I pass them on; instead, I will return them. When traveling, I will carry with me whichever of them I happen to possess. But if I do not wish to carry them about with me, I will not leave them in my house; instead, I will entrust them for safekeeping to my bishop, who holds the same faith and proceeds from the same starting points. If I should also happen to become ill and anticipate death, if I am childless, I will do likewise. But even if I die leaving a child who is unworthy or not yet capable, I will do likewise, for I will entrust them for safekeeping to my bishop, so that if the child, after reaching maturity, should happen to be worthy of the faith, the bishop will return them to the child as a paternal deposit, in accordance with the terms of the solemn attestation.”

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν.
existing_uncertainties.issue: The verified printed wording remains syntactically and semantically unresolved. The force of οὐδ’ ἂν and the relation of the nominative persons to the infinitive lack a secure analysis. The translation provisionally takes τοῦδε as the partitive complement of μεταδοῦναι, referring to the material transmitted, and χάριν as expressing favor or motive. Alternatively, τοῦδε could refer to the unworthy person and be associated with χάριν in the sense ‘for this one’s sake,’ or χάριν could attach in another way. The wording does not demonstrate textual corruption, but no complete English reconstruction is secure.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: εἰ δὲ μὴ βουληθῶ μεθ’ ἑαυτοῦ αὐτὰ περιφέρειν
existing_uncertainties.issue: The reflexive ἑαυτοῦ has a first-person referent supplied by βουληθῶ and the surrounding first-person discourse. This is treated as a possible reflexive usage, not as evidence of textual corruption.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: παρακαταθήσομαι·,
existing_uncertainties.issue: The selected edition prints a middle dot immediately followed by a comma. This is an editorial punctuation anomaly and does not affect the clause’s meaning.

review_findings.source_quote: ἄλλως δὲ οὐδ’ ἂν τέκνον ἢ ἀδελφὸς ἢ φίλος ἢ ἄλλως πως ποτὲ γένους μοι ἀνήκων, ἐάνπερ ἀνάξιος ᾖ, τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν, ὡς οὐ προσῆκεν.
review_findings.english_quote: Otherwise—not even a child or a brother or a friend or anyone ever related to me in any other way, if indeed he is unworthy—not to pass on any of this as a favor, since it is not proper.
review_findings.issue: The English preserves a fragment but does not establish a secure correspondence between its grammatical relationships and those of the supplied Greek. The construction with οὐδ’ ἂν and the nominative persons lacks an expressed governing predicate; the relationship of τοῦδε, μεταδοῦναι, and χάριν remains unresolved. In particular, 'any of this as a favor' combines two provisional interpretations that cannot presently be certified. Consequently, complete propositional coverage, absence of added meaning, and the scope of the opening negation cannot be affirmed. The draft correctly discloses this problem, but disclosure does not make the rendering acceptable. The supplied print verification establishes the wording, not its interpretation; this is not demonstrated OCR error or textual corruption.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Keep publication blocked pending a defensible grammatical and lexical analysis of the supplied sentence, particularly οὐδ’ ἂν and τοῦδε μὴ μεταδοῦναι χάριν. Preserve the unresolved alternatives explicitly rather than inventing a finite predicate or silently changing word division. If an emendation is proposed, distinguish its exact Greek wording from the supplied reading and provide supporting evidence. No replacement English is accepted at this stage.

review_findings.issue: ὑποπτεύσαι expresses suspicion or apprehension. 'Anticipate death' can suggest a firmer expectation and does not clearly preserve that speculative force.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Consider 'suspect that I may die' within the conditional sentence. This proposed wording requires fresh review in context.

review_findings.issue: The immediate context concerns property entrusted to a bishop and its eventual return to a qualified child. The construction ἄξιος τῆς πίστεως therefore strongly supports worthiness of trust, rather than worthiness of the religious faith. The note acknowledges 'trust' but privileges 'faith' primarily because the setting is ecclesial; that does not adequately address the fiduciary context or the construction itself. The earlier reference to the bishop holding the same faith need not determine this occurrence's sense.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Compare the proposed main-text rendering 'worthy of trust' with 'worthy of the faith'. Document the contextual reason for distinguishing this occurrence from τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχοντι πίστιν, and retain the religious-faith interpretation as an alternative if it remains viable. Any revised clause must undergo fresh review.

greek.source_text: ὅθεν ἐγώ, κύριέ μου Ἰάκωβε, αὐτοῦ ταῦτα εἰπόντος ὑποσχόμενος οὐκ ὤκνησα, ὡς ἐκελεύσθην, τὸ πολὺ τῶν κατὰ πόλιν λόγων τῶν ἤδη σοι προγραφέντων καὶ ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ διαπεμφθέντων ἐν βίβλοις ἐπὶ κεφαλαίων ποιῆσαι ὥσπερ σημείου χάριν καὶ οὕτως διαπέμψαι σοι, ἐπιγράψαντα Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή. πλὴν τοῦ ἐκτιθέναι ὡς ἐκελεύσθην ἄρξομαι.

resolved_passages.provisional_english: Therefore I, my lord James, after he had said these things and I had made my promise, did not hesitate, as I had been commanded, to present in outline the greater part of the discourses from city to city, which had already been written to you beforehand and sent by him in books, as a kind of reminder, and in this form to send them to you, giving the work the title “Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Sojourn-Preachings.” But I will begin to set it out as I was commanded.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ἐπιγράψαντα
existing_uncertainties.issue: The accusative participle is syntactically marked with the first-person subject of οὐκ ὤκνησα. It may agree with an understood accusative subject of the dependent infinitives. The nominative ἐπιγράψας would be a conjectural normalization, not an established correction to the supplied reading.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή
existing_uncertainties.issue: The adjective ἐπιδημίων directly and attributively qualifies κηρυγμάτων; it is not an explicit temporal phrase modifying an act of preaching. Its lexical association with presence in a place, sojourning, or visiting supports understanding the preachings as characterized by Peter’s sojourns or visits, and the preceding description of discourses κατὰ πόλιν gives contextual support to a visit-associated sense. Nevertheless, the adjective can also bear a local or public sense connected with being in a place or among its people, and the title does not specify whether the relationship is temporal, circumstantial, or classificatory. “Sojourn-Preachings” is therefore a deliberately source-qualified provisional rendering, while alternatives such as “preachings during Peter’s sojourns,” “visit-preachings,” or “local/public preachings” remain unresolved. No change to the supplied Greek is proposed.

review_findings.source_quote: Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή
review_findings.issue: The compound preserves ἐπιδημίων as qualifying the preachings, and the preceding city-by-city description supports an association with Peter's visits or stays. Nevertheless, the adjective's precise force remains unresolved between visit-associated and local/public senses. The existing disclosure identifies this as publication-blocking. The provisional compound does not itself resolve the lexical uncertainty, and no defect in the verified Greek has been established.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Provide separate, cited lexical evidence for ἐπιδήμιος in comparable literary contexts, explicitly distinguishing evidence for the adjective from evidence merely for cognate nouns or verbs. Assess that evidence against the supplied title and preceding description. Retain the provisional title and alternatives pending assessment; any replacement requires fresh review. Keep the discussion of ἐπιγράψαντα separate as a syntactic feature: ἐπιγράψας remains a proposed normalization, not an established correction.

greek.source_text: οἱ μὲν οὖν τῆς ἐκκλησίας διάκονοι τοῦ ἐπισκόπου συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι ἔστωσαν ὀφθαλμοί, ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν, ἵνα νουθεσίᾳ καταληφθεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ προκαθεζομένου τάχα οὐ μὴ τελέσῃ τὸ ἁμάρτημα· τοὺς λειποτάκτας ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν, τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν, ὅπως τὰς ἑκάστοτε τῇ καρδίᾳ προσπιπτούσας ἀθυμίας ἔκ τε βιωτικῶν συνπτώσεων καὶ ὁμιλιῶν κακῶν λόγῳ ἀληθείας καθαίρεσθαι δύνωνται· ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται. τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας μανθανέτωσαν καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται, καὶ τὰ δέοντα ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ προκαθεζομένου γνώμῃ παρεχέτωσαν· τοῦτο δὲ κἂν λάθρα αὐτοῦ ποιῶσιν, οὐχ ἁμαρτάνουσιν. ταῦτα μὲν οὖν καὶ τὰ τούτοις ὅμοια οἱ διάκονοι προνοείτωσαν.

resolved_passages.provisional_english: The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, roaming about discerningly and closely examining the conduct of each person in the church—who is about to sin—so that, when caught through admonition by the one who presides, that person perhaps may not carry the sin through at all. They should bring back those who desert their posts, so that those who assemble do not fail to listen to the discourses, and so that they may be able, by the word of truth, to clear away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For whenever they have lain fallow for a long time, they become material for fire. They should also find out who are sick in the flesh and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that they may present themselves; and they should provide what is necessary according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should attend to these and similar matters.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν
existing_uncertainties.issue: The syntax permits materially different analyses. The main text takes τοὺς συνερχομένους as the accusative subject of ἐπιλείπειν and ἐπακούειν as its complement: “so that those who assemble do not fail to listen.” Alternatively, ἐπακούειν may depend on συνερχομένους, yielding “those who assemble to listen,” while intransitive ἐπιλείπειν means that they do not fall away or become wanting. A further alternative makes the deacons the unexpressed subject of transitive ἐπιλείπειν: “so that they do not abandon those who assemble to listen to the discourses.” The consulted lexical evidence attests senses such as leaving behind, failing someone, becoming wanting, and construction with an infinitive, but it does not settle Clement’s syntax. The supplied Greek is not being treated as corrupt.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: συνπτώσεων
existing_uncertainties.issue: The supplied edition has the unassimilated spelling συνπτώσεων. The normalized spelling συμπτώσεων represents the same word and meaning; this is a disclosed orthographic feature, not evidence of OCR corruption.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται
existing_uncertainties.issue: The plural subject of χερσεύσωσιν and γίνονται is not explicit. It may refer to the people who assemble and listen, to the discouragements, or to people understood through the image of land lying fallow. The translation retains the unresolved pronoun “they.”

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται
existing_uncertainties.issue: The precise force of προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται remain uncertain. The sick may be brought to the multitude’s attention and then present themselves, or members of the previously unaware multitude may present themselves, perhaps by coming to the sick. “Visit them” would make that latter contextual inference explicit, but neither a visitation sense nor an object meaning “them” is separately expressed. The supplied reading is being translated provisionally, not emended.

review_findings.source_quote: ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις τίς μέλλει ἁμαρτάνειν
review_findings.english_quote: closely examining the conduct of each person in the church—who is about to sin—
review_findings.issue: τίς introduces the inquiry into who is about to sin. The English dashes make the phrase liable to be read as a relative description of each person instead. The lexical note recognizes the interrogative, but the main wording does not clearly convey it.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Use “closely examining the conduct of each person in the church to see who is about to sin.” This proposed wording requires fresh review.

review_findings.source_quote: τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν
review_findings.english_quote: so that those who assemble do not fail to listen to the discourses
review_findings.issue: This remains a possible interpretation, not an established analysis. The accusative τοὺς συνερχομένους can be analyzed as the subject or object of ἐπιλείπειν, and ἐπακούειν can attach to ἐπιλείπειν or συνερχομένους. The cited Antiphon example establishes an infinitival construction but, with its dative pronoun and negative infinitive, does not settle these particular attachments. The existing source_issues disclosure is appropriate, but its publication-blocking meaning question remains unresolved.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Keep the rendering explicitly provisional. Compare the three analyses against closer syntactic parallels, preferably from this author: assembled people failing to listen; people assembled to listen falling away; and the deacons not abandoning those assembled to listen. Retain the alternatives in source_issues and do not treat the construction as corrupt or any replacement as already accepted.

review_findings.source_quote: καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται
review_findings.english_quote: and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that they may present themselves
review_findings.issue: The rendering is plausible, but the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται is not established. The sick people and members of the collectively expressed multitude remain possible referents. Evidence that passive ἐπιφαίνω can mean appearing or presenting oneself does not identify who appears here or establish a visit to the sick. The note correctly discloses this uncertainty; it does not resolve the meaning question that the draft marks as publication-blocking.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected Greek and the unresolved subject in source_issues. Seek contextual or author-specific parallels before accepting a subject-specific rendering. “May appear” or “may present themselves” can remain provisional; “visit them” would require an explicit statement that the visitation and its object are contextual inferences.

Distinguish ordinary ambiguity from corruption. Do not assume the provisional English or automated finding is correct. Any proposed revision must be source-checked again.

greek.source_text: εὐσταθείτωσαν οὖν οἱ ἐπιβάται ἑδραῖοι ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων καθεζόμενοι τόπων, ἵνα μὴ τῇ ἀταξίᾳ σεισμὸν ἢ ἑτεροκλινίαν παρέχωσιν. οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοὺς μισθοὺς ὑπομιμνησκέτωσαν. οἱ διάκονοι μηδὲν ἀμελείτωσαν ὧν ἐπιστεύθησαν. οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ὥσπερ ’ναῦται καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς τὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ. ὁ ἐπίσκοπος ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω. ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης φιλείσθω καὶ μόνος περὶ ὧν λέγει πιστευέσθω. οἱ δὲ πάντες τῷ θεῷ περὶ τοῦ οὐρίᾳ πλέειν προσευχέσθωσαν. οἱ πλέοντες πᾶσαν θλίψιν προσδοκάτωσαν ὡς μέγαν καὶ ταραχώδη βυθὸν παραπλέοντες, τὸν κόσμον· ὁτὲ μὲν ἀθυμοῦντες, διωκόμενοι, σκορπιζόμενοι, πεινῶντες, διψῶντες, γυμνητεύοντες, στενοχωρούμενοι, καὶ πάλιν ὁτὲ μὲν ἐνούμενοι, συναλιζόμενοι, ἡσυχάζοντες· ἀλλὰ καὶ ναυτιῶντες, ἰλιγγιῶντες, ἀπερῶντες (τουτέστιν ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰ παραπτώματα ὥσπερ νοσοποιοὺς χολάς, τὰς ἐκ πικρίας ἁμαρτίας λέγω καὶ τὰ ἐξ ἐπιθυμιῶν ἀτάκτων σωρευθέντα κακά, ἅτινα τῷ ὁμολογῆσαι ὥσπερ ἀπεράσαντες κουφίζεσθε τῆς νόσου, προσιέμενοι τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν).

resolved_passages.provisional_english: The passengers, then, should remain steady, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiters should give reminders of the rewards. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what each person needs. The bishop, as a bow officer keeping watch, should respond to the words of the helmsman alone. The Messiah, as Savior-helmsman, should be loved, and he alone should be trusted regarding what he says. All should pray to God that they may sail with a fair wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction as they sail beside a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, naked, and distressed, and again at another time united, gathered together, and at rest, but also seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing their offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—by which I mean the sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive care).

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ὥσπερ ’ναῦται
existing_uncertainties.issue: The mark printed before ναῦται is not explained by ordinary elision, but this does not establish that it is accidental. Its editorial or typographic function remains unresolved; the translation treats it provisionally as nonlexical without altering the supplied transcription.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς τὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ
existing_uncertainties.issue: The selected transcription reads τὰ. The recorded high-resolution crop review of a second copy of the same edition preserves the first letter’s horizontal head-bar and bent lower stroke, resolving an earlier transcription as -ὰ that resulted from a disconnected printing impression. This is a confirmed crop correction within the transcription record, not an unverified emendation of the supplied Greek.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς
existing_uncertainties.issue: The mark printed before ἐγρηγορὼς is not required by the apparent syntax and is not explained by ordinary elision, but it may be an intentional editorial or typographic feature. The translation treats it provisionally as nonlexical without presenting an unmarked Greek form as an established correction.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω
existing_uncertainties.issue: The exact action expressed by ἀντιβαλλέτω remains uncertain. The attested conversational exchange sense supports “respond to the words,” while “echo” or “repeat the words” may fit the shipboard command context. “Relay the words” more specifically implies onward transmission and is not directly established by the consulted evidence. The comparison or collation sense of ἀντιβάλλω is also attested generally but is less readily intelligible here. No alteration of the supplied Greek is proposed.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης φιλείσθω
existing_uncertainties.issue: One ὡς governs the adjacent nouns σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης without καί. The main rendering “Savior-helmsman” preserves both as a combined designation. Possible interpretive alternatives include “as Savior, helmsman,” “as the saving helmsman,” and the explicitly coordinated “as Savior and helmsman,” but the last introduces a conjunction absent from the Greek. The exact grammatical relationship between the two designations remains uncertain.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ἐνούμενοι
existing_uncertainties.issue: The verified printed form ἐνούμενοι has smooth breathing. “United” understands it as the unity verb conventionally written ἑνόω, whose corresponding participle is ἑνούμενοι. The supplied Greek is retained; this is a disclosed orthographic identification, not an established OCR error or a silently normalized reading.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ἀπερῶντες
existing_uncertainties.issue: The uncommon form is interpreted as vomiting or purging because the author immediately explains it through the expulsion of disease-producing bile and later uses ἀπεράσαντες in the same comparison. The general purgative sense is contextually strong, but the exact lexical formation remains uncertain.

review_findings.source_quote: ὁ ἐπίσκοπος ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω
review_findings.english_quote: The bishop, as a bow officer keeping watch, should respond to the words of the helmsman alone.
review_findings.issue: “Respond to” has some support from the conversational sense of ἀντιβάλλω, but the cited reciprocal exchange construction does not establish this particular action. Here τοὺς λόγους is the direct object, and τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου identifies whose words they are; no interlocutor or onward recipient is expressed. Responding, exchanging, repeating, and relaying therefore cannot be treated as interchangeable established meanings. The draft appropriately records alternatives, but its explicitly publication-blocking lexical question remains open.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Keep “respond to” provisional rather than certifying it as the settled sense. Compare author-specific uses and relevant nautical command language before choosing among responding, exchanging, or repeating the helmsman’s words. Onward transmission in “relay” remains an additional contextual inference. Preserve the uncertainty in source_issues; this is a meaning problem, not demonstrated corruption or a reason to alter the printed mark before ἐγρηγορὼς. Any selected replacement needs fresh review.

greek.source_text: ἔνια δὲ καὶ ἀφ᾽ ἑαυτῶν νοεῖν ὀφείλετε διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν μὴ δύνασθαι ἐν φανερῷ λέγειν διὰ τὰς ἐπιβουλάς, οἷον ἐὰν ἐχθραίνῃ τινί, μὴ ἀναμένετε αὐτὸν εἰπεῖν τῷδε μὴ προσαμιλλᾶσθαι, ἀλλὰ φρονίμως ἕπεσθε αὐτοῦ τῷ βουλήματι, ἐχθροὶ γινόμενοι οἷς ἐχθραίνει καὶ μὴ ὁμιλοῦντες οἷς μὴ ὁμιλεῖ· ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται, τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας. εἰ δέ τις φίλος μένει οἷς αὐτὸς ἐχθραίνει, καὶ λαλεῖ οἷς αὐτὸς οὐχ ὁμιλεῖ, εἷς ἐστὶν καὶ αὐτὸς τῶν ὀλοθρεύειν θελόντων τὴν ἐκκλησίαν· τῷ γὰρ σώματι συνὼν ὑμῖν, τῇ γνώμῃ μὴ ὢν μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν, καθ᾽ ὑμῶν ἐστίν, πολλῷ χείρων τῶν ἔξωθεν φαινομένων ἐχθρῶν, μετὰ δοκούσης φιλίας σκορπίζων τοὺς ἔσω.

resolved_passages.provisional_english: But you should also understand some things on your own, because he cannot speak openly on account of the plots. For example, if he is hostile to someone, do not wait for him to say, “Do not associate with this person.” Instead, prudently follow his intention, becoming enemies of those to whom he is hostile and not associating with those with whom he does not associate, so that each person, pressing his claim to have everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him and heeding his discourse. But if anyone remains a friend to those to whom he is hostile and speaks with those with whom he does not associate, he himself is also one of those who want to destroy the church. For although he is joined with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose, he is against you—far worse than the manifest enemies from outside, scattering those inside under the guise of friendship.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται
existing_uncertainties.issue: The referent of αὐτόν and the relationship expressed by διαλλάττων remain unresolved. The presiding leader is the most continuously salient singular masculine referent: the preceding clauses repeatedly use αὐτός and αὐτοῦ for him, whereas the intervening οἷς is plural and denotes those to whom he is hostile. Contextually, communal withdrawal could compel an alienated person who wants everyone as friends to reconcile the leader or win him over. Grammatically, however, αὐτόν is the direct object of active διαλλάττων; the construction explicitly presents him as the affected person but does not state the other party to the reconciliation. It can therefore be understood as reconciling the leader, winning him over, or elliptically effecting reconciliation with him. A less likely but possible interpretation takes αὐτόν as another alienated person. The translation retains the pronoun and direct-object construction because the supplied wording does not settle these materially different relationships.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας
existing_uncertainties.issue: The possessive αὐτοῦ most naturally continues the paragraph’s recurring reference to the presiding leader, particularly the earlier αὐτοῦ τῷ βουλήματι, and this reading makes obedience to his discourse the culmination of following his intention. Nevertheless, the immediately preceding αὐτὸν διαλλάττων introduces an unresolved personal referent, and αὐτοῦ can grammatically refer to that same person. If αὐτόν denotes an alienated person rather than the leader, whose discourse is heeded changes accordingly. The main text therefore preserves the neutral pronoun while the antecedent remains unresolved.

review_findings.source_quote: ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται

greek.source_text: πλὴν γινώσκετε πάντες πάντων ὑμῶν πλεῖον κάμνοντα τὸν ἐπίσκοπον, ὅτι ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τὴν αὐτοῦ θλίψιν πάσχει, αὐτὸς δὲ τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν ἑκάστου. διό, ὦ Κλήμης, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν προκαθέσθητι βοηθός, τὰς πάντων φορτισθεὶς φροντίδας. ὅθεν τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς. ἀλλὰ θάρρει καὶ γενναίως φέρε ὡς εἰδὼς ὅτι ἀποδώσει σοι ὁ θεὸς εἰς τὸν λιμένα τῆς ἀναπαύσεως καταντήσαντι τὸ μέγιστον τῶν ἀγαθῶν, ἀναφαίρετον μισθόν, καθότι ὑπὲρ τῆς τῶν πάντων ’σωτηρίας τὸν μείζονα ἀνεδέξω κάματον. ὥστε ἐάν σε πολλοὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν διὰ τὴν ἐπ’ ἄκρον δικαιοσύνην μισήσωσιν, τὸ αὐτῶν μὲν μῖσος οὐδέν σε βλάψει, ἡ δὲ τοῦ δικαίου θεοῦ φιλία πολύ σε ὀνήσει. ὥστε πειρῶ τὸν ἐξ ἀδικίας γινόμενον ἔπαινον ἀποσείεσθαι, διὰ δὲ δικαίαν διοίκησιν τὸν ἐκ χριστοῦ ἐπωφελῆ θηρεύειν ἔπαινον.

resolved_passages.provisional_english: Nevertheless, all of you know that the bishop labors more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, take your place at the head as a helper to each person, as far as you are able, burdened with the cares of everyone. Hence I know that, in undertaking to oversee you, I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and bear it nobly, knowing that when you have reached the harbor of rest, God will repay you with the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because you undertook the greater toil for the salvation of all. Thus, if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise arising from injustice, but through righteous administration to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς
existing_uncertainties.issue: The assignment of subjects and object remains uncertain. On the analysis selected in the translation, the articular infinitive τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν is the complement of ἀναδέξασθαι, Peter remains the unexpressed subject of both infinitives, and σέ is the direct object of οἰκονομεῖν: Peter undertakes to oversee Clement. This is supported grammatically by the continued first-person perspective and the nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς. Alternatively, σέ may be the accusative subject of οἰκονομεῖν, yielding “your administering”; Peter would then undertake the arrangement that Clement administer, an interpretation contextually attractive after Clement’s commission. A further, less explicit analysis makes Clement the subject of ἀναδέξασθαι as well, so that Clement undertakes the administration, but the change of subject is not overtly marked. The image-checked supplied reading does not adjudicate among these analyses and does not itself establish corruption.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: ’σωτηρίας
existing_uncertainties.issue: The supplied print places a raised apostrophe before σωτηρίας although no elision is apparent. Omitting it would be an orthographic normalization and would not change the translated meaning.

review_findings.source_quote: τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς
review_findings.english_quote: Hence I know that, in undertaking to oversee you, I have received a favor, not given one.
review_findings.issue: The draft makes Peter undertake the oversight of Clement. The stronger contextual analysis takes Clement as the subject of the infinitival undertaking: Clement undertakes to administer, and Peter regards that undertaking as a favor received. The nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς establish Peter as the recipient rather than giver of the favor; they do not establish him as the subject of the embedded infinitives. The draft therefore assigns an administrative relationship that the supplied wording does not securely establish.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Proposed replacement, not yet accepted: “Hence I know that, in your undertaking to administer, I have received a favor, not given one.” Review this proposal afresh after separately documenting the grammatical relationships among the articular infinitival expression, σέ, χάριν, and οἶδα.

review_findings.english_quote: A further, less explicit analysis makes Clement the subject of ἀναδέξασθαι as well, so that Clement undertakes the administration, but the change of subject is not overtly marked.
review_findings.issue: The source_issues note overlooks σέ as an overt possible accusative subject of the entire infinitival expression and consequently misranks the alternatives. The first-person subject of οἶδα must be distinguished from the subject of the embedded infinitives. The assignment of administration remains an unresolved source-meaning issue requiring separate grammatical evidence. The image-checked print establishes the supplied wording, not the interpretation; no corruption has been demonstrated.
review_findings.suggested_revision: Provide a separate grammatical assessment, supported by cited comparable Greek constructions, of σέ as subject of the entire infinitival expression versus object of οἰκονομεῖν. Rewrite the disclosure to reflect that evidence and preserve any remaining alternatives. Do not propose a Greek correction merely to regularize the construction. Keep the passage blocked pending that assessment and fresh review of the English.

greek.source_text: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἐν μέσῳ ἐπὶ πάντων μοι τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιθεὶς εἰς τὴν αὐτοῦ καθέδραν καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν. καθεσθέντι δὲ τοῦτό μοι εὐθέως ἔφη Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν καὶ ὡς ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς μέχρι τοῦ νῦν συνώδευσάς μοι, ἐπακούων τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων, ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς. οὔτε γὰρ λίαν αὐτὸν λυπήσει τοῦτο, εἰδότα ὅτι ὃ πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν εὐσεβῶς ἀπεδόμην, μεγίστης δὲ παραμυθίας τεύξεται, μαθὼν ὅτι μετ᾽ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν· πλάνος γὰρ ὁμιλία τῶν ἀκουόντων ὄχλων ἀναιρεῖ τὰς ψυχάς.

resolved_passages.provisional_english: After saying these things, there in the midst before everyone, he laid his hands on me and urged me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are present with me, I ask you that, whenever I depart from this life here—as is owed to me—you not hesitate to send James, the Lord’s brother, a concise written account extending even to your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, listening to the words and deeds proclaimed by me from city to city, and then, toward the end, also to make known the cause of my death, as I said beforehand. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that I have piously paid what I was inevitably bound to suffer. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me it was not to an unlearned man—one ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule—that the teacher’s chair was entrusted. For misleading discourse destroys the souls of the crowds who hear it.”

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν
existing_uncertainties.issue: The printed period separates the infinitive from the finite verb that most naturally governs it. The translation construes the words together while preserving the period as an editorial feature of the supplied edition; this punctuation does not by itself demonstrate textual corruption.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν καὶ ὡς ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς μέχρι τοῦ νῦν συνώδευσάς μοι, ἐπακούων τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων, ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς
existing_uncertainties.issue: The relationships among Ἀξιῶ σε, ὅπως, the resumed σέ, the infinitives διαπέμψαι and δηλῶσαι, and the final μὴ ὀκνήσῃς remain syntactically unsettled. The main translation takes Ἀξιῶ σε with the ὅπως request, treats μὴ ὀκνήσῃς as the finite conclusion governing both infinitival instructions, and understands the sense as “I ask you … not to hesitate to send … and then, toward the end, also to make known …”. The final position of μὴ ὀκνήσῃς and the coordination of the two requested acts support that scope. The second σέ is then read as a resumptive accusative subject after the intervening temporal clause, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with it, although a complementary infinitive with the same subject as ὀκνήσῃς would ordinarily omit that subject. Alternatively, σέ may be the object of διαπέμψαι, “send yourself to James,” though a reflexive form would be more expected; or μὴ ὀκνήσῃς may attach explicitly only to δηλῶσαι, leaving διαπέμψαι more directly dependent on the earlier request. The supplied wording and image-checked punctuation do not settle these alternatives or independently establish corruption.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν
existing_uncertainties.issue: The scope of the first οὐκ remains uncertain. The main translation takes οὐκ as excluding the whole described recipient from the entrusting: it was not to an unlearned man—one ignorant of life-giving words and explicitly described by οὐκ εἰδώς as not knowing the church’s rule—that the chair was entrusted. This reading fits the delayed verb ἐπιστεύθη and the stated consolation obtained from learning who succeeded Peter. Formally, however, οὐκ stands immediately before ἀμαθής and can locally produce “a not-unlearned man,” after which the positive participle ἀγνοῶν and the explicitly negated οὐκ εἰδώς create a difficult coordination. The conjunctions καί do not independently establish that the first negation distributes across all the descriptions. Both negations are preserved in the translation, but the syntax does not securely determine whether the first negates only ἀμαθής or the larger proposition concerning the recipient of the chair.

existing_uncertainties.source_quote: κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς
existing_uncertainties.issue: The printed period interrupts the description before οὐκ εἰδώς. The translation treats the participle as continuing the description while retaining the period as an editorial feature of the supplied edition; the punctuation alone is not evidence of textual corruption or a resolution of the negation’s scope.
